title: Mars Sedimentary Rocks
description: Send a robotic rover to Mars to investigate sedimentary rocks, analyze their chemistry and mineralogy, and identify geological evidence of an ancient watery environment. Select instruments capable of studying fine-grained rocks and subsurface structure while keeping the rover within its mass, power, communications, and launch constraints.
primary_objective: Characterize sedimentary rocks and geological formations.
constraints: Balance instrument mass, electrical power and sample storage.

title: Lunar Polar Ice
description: Send a robotic rover to the lunar south polar region to search for hydrogen-rich material, identify possible water ice and other volatiles, and investigate subsurface deposits. Build a rover able to operate under difficult illumination and thermal conditions while powering drilling and analytical instruments.
primary_objective: Search for and characterize polar water ice.
constraints: Plan for limited sunlight, instrument power and cold polar conditions.

title: Exoplanet Characterization
description: Launch a space telescope designed to detect and characterize faint planets near bright stars. Suppress stellar glare, maintain extremely precise pointing, collect spectra of selected planetary targets, and return enough data to study atmospheric composition.
primary_objective: Search for exoplanets and characterize candidate atmospheres.
recommended_orbit: 200 km parking orbit  /  Sun-Earth L2 transfer (~1.5 million km)
constraints: Prioritize pointing stability, thermal control and clean optical observations.

title: Galaxy Evolution Survey
description: Launch an infrared space observatory able to image large regions of the sky and obtain spectra from distant galaxies. Study how galaxies formed and evolved while managing extremely high scientific data volume.
primary_objective: Study the evolution of distant galaxies.
recommended_orbit: 200 km parking orbit  /  Sun-Earth L2 transfer (~1.5 million km)
constraints: Balance observation depth, survey coverage, cooling and downlink capacity.

title: Asteroid Reconnaissance
description: Send an autonomous interplanetary spacecraft to rendezvous with a near-Earth asteroid. Map its shape and surface, measure mineral and thermal properties, and characterize the object using cameras, spectroscopy, and laser topography.
primary_objective: Map an asteroid's surface, topography and composition.
constraints: Provide reliable deep-space communications and precise attitude control.

title: Comet Investigation
description: Send an interplanetary probe to a comet and investigate its nucleus, dust environment, and composition. Survive the encounter, collect imaging and dust measurements, analyze material around the comet, and transmit observations to Earth.
primary_objective: Image the nucleus during a close flyby and measure the composition and flux of cometary dust.
constraints: Account for changing solar power, dust exposure and deep-space downlink.

title: Orbital Station Refueling
description: Deliver propellant to an orbital station. Design an automated cargo spacecraft able to carry a useful fuel load, rendezvous, dock safely, and transfer propellant while preserving enough fuel for its own orbital maneuvers.
primary_objective: Rendezvous and dock at the station. Transfer at least 800 kg of fuel while keeping a separate maneuver reserve.
recommended_orbit: 400 km low Earth orbit  /  station rendezvous
constraints: Balance delivered cargo mass, propulsion reserves and docking compatibility.

title: Earth Atmosphere Observatory
description: Launch a satellite to repeatedly measure the composition and temperature structure of Earth's atmosphere. Select instruments and an orbit that provide broad global coverage while maintaining adequate power, storage, calibration, and downlink capacity.
constraints: Trade observation coverage against generated data and available downlink.

title: Earth Imaging Satellite
description: Deploy an Earth-observation satellite capable of collecting useful multispectral imagery over large regions of the planet. Balance spatial resolution, swath width, revisit time, pointing accuracy, storage, and communications.
primary_objective: Capture useful images of Earth's surface.
constraints: Higher resolution increases pointing, storage and downlink requirements.

title: Navigation Constellation Satellite
description: Design and deploy one operational satellite for a GPS-like navigation constellation. Place it in the correct medium-Earth orbit, provide highly stable timing, transmit navigation signals, and maintain enough power and propulsion for long-term service.
primary_objective: Provide precise navigation timing and signals.
constraints: A single satellite cannot provide full GPS-like coverage; this is a constellation element.
